Graphics Assets Integrate the graphics assets into the game so that they display properly across different mobile phones and tablets with different aspect ratios and screen resolutions. 3. Animation Integrate the animations and write the necessary code to make them fluid and smooth. 4. Game Physics Program the game mechanics and physics, including jumping, falling, breaking objects, collisions, and other gameplay interactions. 5. User Interface (UI) Program the game's UI elements, such as Play, Score, Pause, Replay, Health Status, Game Items/Inventory, HUD, and other interface elements. 6. Touch and Gesture Controls Develop and implement touch and gesture controls for navigation and gameplay. 7. Sound Effects and Music Integrate the music, sound effects, and other audio files into the game. 8. Game File Size Keep the final game size as small as reasonably possible, because players are generally less willing to download games with unnecessarily large file sizes. 9. Optimization Optimize the game for performance and memory usage across a range of mobile devices. This includes reducing unnecessary CPU and GPU workload, maintaining a stable frame rate, minimizing memory usage, and keeping the code structure efficient and maintainable. The game should not unnecessarily depend on a constant internet connection. Unity's own documentation emphasizes profiling and optimization for mobile because Android and iOS devices vary considerably in performance. 10. Android and iOS Release Develop the game so that it can be published on both Android and iOS. 11. In-App Purchases Implement in-app purchases. 12. In-App Advertising Implement in-app advertising. 13. If you live elsewhere, you will need to relocate to Chattogram at your own cost within 30 days of an offer. Applications without links to 2 projects will not be reviewed. About PEN Global PEN Global is part of PEN Group, a transnational education group operating across the UK, Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Our Chattogram office builds the web and mobile products used by students, agents and staff across the group, working every day with the UK product team. The role You will design web and mobile products for the UK product team and own your user flows end to end, working with product managers and developers every day. This is a UX-led role. We care most about how you think: information architecture, user flows, interaction logic, and removing steps users don't need. Visual polish matters, but it comes second to understanding what users are actually trying to do. You will use AI tools every day to explore and prototype faster, and your own judgement to decide what is good enough to ship. We will test exactly that in the hiring process. What you will do • Own user flows: map, question, simplify and defend flows end to end. Every screen needs a clear reason to exist. • Structure before pixels: turn requirements into information architecture, task flows and wireframes before high-fidelity work. • Prototype in Figma : build prototypes that can be tested with real users and handed to developers without ambiguity. • Design with AI: use AI tools to generate and explore options quickly, then refine, correct and validate the output yourself. • Test with users: run usability tests, heuristic reviews and stakeholder interviews, and turn findings into clear, prioritised recommendations. • Remove friction: cut unnecessary steps, clicks, form fields and decisions, and use feedback and data to prove the improvement. • Grow the design system: keep patterns consistent and reusable across products. • Work with developers: review what gets built and give precise, actionable feedback. • Design accessibly: treat accessibility and inclusion as part of the process, not a final checklist. What you need • 3+ years as a UI/UX, UX or Product Designer. This is not a junior role. • 2 projects that show your process: the problem, the user flows, the iterations and the outcome. jobs.title: Computer Vision QA Specialist
jobs.description: In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Computer Vision QA Specialist to review image and video annotations for quality, accuracy, and guideline compliance. You will evaluate annotations such as bounding boxes, segmentation masks, polygons, keypoints, object classes, attributes, and video tracks, identifying missing, incorrect, inconsistent, or poorly placed annotations. You will also make corrections when required, provide clear feedback on quality issues, and communicate unclear cases to the project team. This role requires strong attention to detail, consistency, and the ability to carefully follow detailed computer vision annotation guidelines. This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your computer vision QA work directly helps improve the world’s premier AI models by ensuring that visual training data is accurate, complete, consistent, and aligned with project expectations. Key Responsibilities Review annotation quality: Review image and video annotations for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and adherence to project guidelines. Check annotation outputs: Evaluate bounding boxes, classes, attributes, segmentation masks, polygons, keypoints, image labels, and video tracking outputs. Identify annotation errors: Spot missing objects, incorrect labels, inaccurate boundaries, poor box placement, inconsistent attributes, duplicate annotations, and unclear edge cases. Make corrections when required: Correct annotation issues according to project-specific instructions and quality standards. Provide clear feedback: Document quality issues clearly so annotators or project teams can understand what needs to be improved. Follow project guidelines: Apply detailed annotation rules consistently across tasks, including rules for occlusion, truncation, blur, small objects, overlapping objects, and ambiguous cases. Escalate unclear cases: Communicate questions or uncertain examples to the project team for clarification. Maintain consistent work quality: Complete assigned QA work reliably while maintaining accuracy, consistency, and expected productivity. Your Profile Previous experience with computer vision annotation, image annotation, video annotation, or annotation QA is preferred. Experience reviewing or creating annotations such as bounding boxes, polygons, segmentation masks, keypoints, object classes, attributes, image classification, or video object tracking. Strong attention to detail and ability to identify missing, incorrect, inconsistent, overlapping, mislabeled, or poorly placed annotations. Comfortable working with detailed annotation guidelines, edge-case rules, quality standards, and project-specific instructions. Ability to review image and video data consistently across large batches while maintaining accuracy and speed. Comfortable making corrections when required and explaining annotation errors clearly. Good professional proficiency in English to understand guidelines, communicate questions, and provide written feedback. Able to work independently in an hourly remote workflow and commit consistent working hours based on project needs. Prior experience with annotation platforms such as SuperAnnotate, Labelbox, CVAT, Scale, Appen, Remotasks, Toloka, or similar tools is preferred. jobs.title: Security Officer (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description: Job Description Tiered Approach In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026. Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management. The Operations Team is a key enabler of programme delivery, ensuring the right systems, resources, and processes are in place for results to happen. Working under the leadership of the Operations Advisor, it covers the full range of operational functions administration, procurement, finance, human resources, ICT, and security and collaborates closely with programme teams, extending operational support to partner UN agencies where needed. Its core focus is compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, effective internal controls, and continuous improvement of operational systems, combining sound process management with responsiveness, anticipation of programme needs, and sound judgment. UNDP Bangladesh delivers a diverse programme portfolio spanning democratic governance, climate and environment, and inclusive growth, including operations in geographically remote and security-sensitive areas such as the Chittagong Hill Tracts and coastal, disaster-prone districts. Programme delivery depends on a functioning security risk management framework that enables personnel, partners and communities to operate safely. The Host Government bears primary responsibility for the safety and security of personnel and property of organizations within the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS). UNDSS holds responsibility for United Nations system security risk management in Bangladesh, including the security risk assessments, the security risk management measures, the country security plan, the Security Operations Centre, the warden system and the issuance of advisories. The Country Office security function, working with the UNDP Security Office, the Regional Security Advisor and the Sub-Regional Security Specialist, and with UNDSS, supports UNDP compliance with that framework; it does not substitute for it. Bangladesh has been undergoing a significant political transition since August 2024. National elections and a constitutional referendum held in February 2026 returned a new elected government. The security risk management situational analyses describe the political climate as cautiously stable but fragile, with law-and-order institutions still being reconstituted and primacy for public order returning to the police and civil authorities. UNDP operations fall within seven security risk management areas. The approved general threat assessments rate crime, civil unrest and hazards as substantial or high in the Dhaka Metro, Cox’s Bazar and Chittagong Hill Tracts areas, and the security level in the Dhaka Metro and Chittagong Hill Tracts areas is 3 (Moderate). Duties And Responsibilities Under the overall security accountability of the Resident Representative and the day-to-day supervision of the Operations Advisor, and under the technical supervision of the Sub-Regional Security Specialist for Asia and the Pacific together with the Regional Security Advisor, the Security Officer provides security risk management support to Country Office management to enable effective UNDP programme delivery throughout Bangladesh, within the framework of the UNSMS and UNDP security policies and procedures. The position prepares, analyses and recommends; decisions carrying operational risk consequences are taken by the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative or the Operations Advisor. The incumbent will have the following specific duties and responsibilities: Security risk management and programming support Support the preparation of security risk assessments for UNDP programmes, projects and operations across all areas of assignment, including the Chittagong Hill Tracts and other field locations, and recommend mitigation measures for the approval of the Resident Representative or the Operations Advisor. Support the mainstreaming of security, and its costs, into all stages of programme and project design, implementation and delivery, under the technical guidance of the Regional Security Advisor and the Sub-Regional Security Specialist. Analyse the effect of security factors and trends on programme planning and delivery, and the effect of programme design on stability and security and submit recommendations to management. Prepare inputs for UNDSS for the preparation and periodic update of country and area-specific security risk assessments and related documentation. Support application of the Person-Centred Approach in security risk management to address specific threats, risks or vulnerabilities identified through assessments. Security plans, business continuity and compliance with the UN security framework Support the establishment, maintenance and testing of Country Office security and contingency plans in accordance with the UN Security Policy Manual (SPM) and the country-specific Security Risk Management (SRM) process, in coordination with UNDSS. Ensure that all UNDP personnel, including project personnel and eligible dependants, are captured in the Security Plan maintained by UNDSS, working with the Human Resources and Procurement Units to keep personnel and eligible family member lists current. Prepare security-related inputs to the Country Office Business Continuity Plan, aligned with UNDP Business Continuity Management, Enterprise Risk Management and the UN Country Team Business Continuity Plan. Monitor and report on compliance with Security Risk Management Measures (SRMM) and Residential Security Measures (RSM) for UNDP premises, residences, equipment and personnel, through the UNDP corporate Security Compliance Survey (SCS) online tool. Prepare advice for the Resident Representative and the Operations Advisor on funding requirements under the UN Mandated Security Measures mechanism, reflecting the measures identified through the country-specific SRM process. Coordinate fire safety, first aid, security communications and other security-related training for Country Office personnel, in collaboration with UNDSS. Prepare and process security clearance requests for UNDP personnel travelling to restricted or field areas, for approval by the Operations Advisor. Support to Country Office security personnel, briefing and training Provide day-to-day work direction and technical guidance to the Security Assistant based in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. Deliver orientation, briefings and training to UNDP personnel, national and international, on security guidelines, communication procedures, travel precautions and emergency and curfew arrangements, in coordination with the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS. Ensure that security equipment inventories, communication systems and access control mechanisms are maintained and kept up to date. Identify learning and capacity-building needs of Country Office security personnel and coordinate with the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS on relevant training opportunities. Incident reporting, information and liaison support and support knowledge sharing Provide timely and accurate security advice and briefings to the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative, the Operations Advisor, programme and project managers and visiting personnel. Report immediately all security-related incidents involving UNDP personnel and eligible family members to the Resident Representative, the Operations Advisor, the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS, and support coordinated 24-hour incident response. Support liaison with UNDSS and with security counterparts in other UN agencies. Liaison with national law enforcement, civil authorities and host Government security authorities is conducted through UNDSS or in the company of a designated UNDP staff member. Attend inter-agency security coordination mechanisms, including the Security Cell, the Area Security Management Team and the Security Management Team, in a technical support capacity accompanying the designated UNDP staff member, and prepare the supporting technical inputs and briefing material. Contribute to security-related knowledge networks and professional communities within UNDP and the wider UNSMS. Premises and residential security compliance support Conduct periodic security assessments of UNDP premises, guesthouses, vehicles and equipment, and advise on shortfalls with recommended SRM and RSM measures. Support implementation of physical security and access control measures, including visitor and vehicle screening, for Country Office and project premises. Provide technical support to the designated UNDP staff member on UNDP security requirements in common UN premises, ensuring that the safety and security of personnel remain primary considerations. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Institutional Arrangement The Security Officer works under the overall security accountability of the Resident Representative and the direct day-to-day supervision of the Operations Advisor, with technical supervis

jobs.title: Project Analyst (Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description: Job Description Tiered Approach In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026. Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management. UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programme works toward a country that is inclusive, capable, rule-based, accountable, and transparent, so that all citizens can contribute peacefully to national development. It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. UNDP partners with government, civil society, community, and academic institutions to make public institutions more effective, accountable, and responsive, with particular attention to women, youth, and marginalized and minority groups. The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Phase II (2026–2030), implemented by UNDP Bangladesh in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia, supports the implementation and continued reform of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). Building on more than a decade of engagement, the programme addresses persistent challenges in Bangladesh’s social protection system, including fragmented delivery, coverage and targeting gaps, limited gender responsiveness, and uneven implementation capacity, particularly at the local level. The programme focuses on strengthening social protection governance and delivery systems, with particular attention to lifecycle-based support for poor and vulnerable populations. Through embedded technical assistance, government-led pilots, improved data and monitoring systems, and evidence-based policy support, SSPS Phase II will advance reforms in governance and local delivery, lifecycle social protection, climate-responsive and shock-adaptive social protection, urban and social insurance linkages, and gender equality and disability inclusion. The programme aims to translate policy commitments into effective, inclusive, and fiscally sustainable social protection that contributes to poverty reduction, human development, employment, and resilience. Duties And Responsibilities She/he will have the following specific duties and responsibilities: 1- Lead Project Monitoring, Evaluation, Results Reporting and Adaptive Learning: Lead the design, implementation and periodic review of the Project MEL Plan, Results Framework, indicators, monitoring tools, performance tracking systems and reporting templates. Coordinate monitoring of programme outputs, outcomes, indicators and milestones across the programme’s thematic portfolios, ensuring timely collection, verification, analysis and reporting of quantitative and qualitative data. Conduct and coordinate data quality assessments and maintain robust monitoring databases and performance information to support results-based management and decision-making. Coordinate preparation of Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), DFAT and other donor reports, annual and periodic progress reports, and other corporate reporting requirements. Coordinate project evaluations, reviews and assessments, including preparation and follow-up of management responses and implementation of evaluation recommendations. Produce and coordinate analytical reports, lessons learned, case studies, outcome stories and other evidence products, and facilitate reflection and learning processes to support adaptive programme management and policy dialogue. Provide substantive MEL inputs to technical documents, policy papers, concept notes, research, evaluations and programme design, and strengthen feedback loops between evidence, implementation and management decision-making. Provide technical guidance to project personnel and government counterparts on the effective use and administration of dashboards, digital MEL systems and related information platforms for monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making. 2- Strengthen Evidence Generation, Data Analytics and Digital MEL Systems: Lead the administration, maintenance, enhancement and continuous development of the NSSS M&E Dashboard, NSSS Reform Tracking Dashboard and related digital monitoring and evidence systems in response to evolving social protection policies, programmes and information needs. Provide technical oversight for digital monitoring, reporting and evidence systems, including integration of monitoring data with the Single Registry MIS, government MIS, mobile applications and other interoperable platforms, to support timely, accurate and accessible programme performance information. Coordinate development and enhancement of digital monitoring architecture that connects national, sub-national and local-level social protection data and supports effective local-to-national evidence and feedback loops. Promote data governance, data quality, interoperability, information security and appropriate data protection measures across digital MEL systems and evidence platforms. Apply data analytics and visualization approaches to transform programme, administrative and other relevant data into dashboards, analytical outputs and decision-support information 3- Support Pilot Monitoring, Household Well-being Evidence Generation and Adaptive Learning: Coordinate monitoring and documentation of SSPS programme pilots, ensuring that implementation experience, results, beneficiary-level data and lessons are systematically incorporated into the project MEL system and used for programme improvement. Support mechanisms for capturing, tracking, analysing and reporting grievances and beneficiary feedback, and strengthen the integration of Grievance Redress System (GRS) evidence into monitoring, reporting and learning processes. Analyse local-level, pilot and beneficiary data to identify implementation and service-delivery gaps, inclusion and exclusion issues, targeting challenges and opportunities for institutionalization or scale-up. Support the SSPS policy and MEL interface for the Bangladesh Multidimensional Household Well-being Panel Survey, working with BBS, Cabinet Division, GED and other relevant stakeholders to articulate policy questions and use cases and ensure that survey evidence responds to social protection reform and programme learning needs. Support the use of survey and other pilot evidence for SDG localization, Family Card learning, social protection targeting and programme performance analysis, and development of decision-oriented evidence products and recommendations. Contribute, within the agreed institutional division of responsibilities, to joint technical processes relating to indicator frameworks, data access, privacy and ethics, analysis and publication planning, and methods review and learning. Translate evidence from pilots, beneficiary feedback and the household well-being survey into recommendations, analytical products and learning that support programme adaptation, policy dialogue and potential scale-up. 4- Lead Digital Knowledge, Evidence Platforms And Technology-Enabled Learning Lead the administration, maintenance, security, enhancement and continuous development of the National Website on Social Protection and related digital evidence platforms to support access to monitoring findings, research, dashboards, learning products and social protection knowledge. jobs.description: Job Description Tiered Approach In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026. Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management. UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programme works toward a country that is inclusive, capable, rule-based, accountable, and transparent, so that all citizens can contribute peacefully to national development. It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. UNDP partners with government, civil society, community, and academic institutions to make public institutions more effective, accountable, and responsive, with particular attention to women, youth, and marginalized and minority groups. The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Phase II (2026–2030), implemented by UNDP Bangladesh in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia, supports the implementation and continued reform of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). Building on more than a decade of engagement, the programme addresses persistent challenges in Bangladesh’s social protection system, including fragmented delivery, coverage and targeting gaps, limited gender responsiveness, and uneven implementation capacity, particularly at the local level. The programme focuses on strengthening social protection governance and delivery systems, with particular attention to lifecycle-based support for poor and vulnerable populations. Through embedded technical assistance, government-led pilots, improved data and monitoring systems, and evidence-based policy support, SSPS Phase II will advance reforms in governance and local delivery, lifecycle social protection, climate-responsive and shock-adaptive social protection, urban and social insurance linkages, and gender equality and disability inclusion. The programme aims to translate policy commitments into effective, inclusive, and fiscally sustainable social protection that contributes to poverty reduction, human development, employment, and resilience. Duties And Responsibilities She/he will have the following specific duties and responsibilities: 1- Lead Project Monitoring, Evaluation, Results Reporting and Adaptive Learning: Lead the design, implementation and periodic review of the Project MEL Plan, Results Framework, indicators, monitoring tools, performance tracking systems and reporting templates. Coordinate monitoring of programme outputs, outcomes, indicators and milestones across the programme’s thematic portfolios, ensuring timely collection, verification, analysis and reporting of quantitative and qualitative data. Conduct and coordinate data quality assessments and maintain robust monitoring databases and performance information to support results-based management and decision-making. Coordinate preparation of Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), DFAT and other donor reports, annual and periodic progress reports, and other corporate reporting requirements. Coordinate project evaluations, reviews and assessments, including preparation and follow-up of management responses and implementation of evaluation recommendations. Produce and coordinate analytical reports, lessons learned, case studies, outcome stories and other evidence products, and facilitate reflection and learning processes to support adaptive programme management and policy dialogue. Provide substantive MEL inputs to technical documents, policy papers, concept notes, research, evaluations and programme design, and strengthen feedback loops between evidence, implementation and management decision-making. Provide technical guidance to project personnel and government counterparts on the effective use and administration of dashboards, digital MEL systems and related information platforms for monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making. 2- Strengthen Evidence Generation, Data Analytics and Digital MEL Systems: Lead the administration, maintenance, enhancement and continuous development of the NSSS M&E Dashboard, NSSS Reform Tracking Dashboard and related digital monitoring and evidence systems in response to evolving social protection policies, programmes and information needs. Provide technical oversight for digital monitoring, reporting and evidence systems, including integration of monitoring data with the Single Registry MIS, government MIS, mobile applications and other interoperable platforms, to support timely, accurate and accessible programme performance information. Coordinate development and enhancement of digital monitoring architecture that connects national, sub-national and local-level social protection data and supports effective local-to-national evidence and feedback loops. Promote data governance, data quality, interoperability, information security and appropriate data protection measures across digital MEL systems and evidence platforms. Apply data analytics and visualization approaches to transform programme, administrative and other relevant data into dashboards, analytical outputs and decision-support information 3- Support Pilot Monitoring, Household Well-being Evidence Generation and Adaptive Learning: Coordinate monitoring and documentation of SSPS programme pilots, ensuring that implementation experience, results, beneficiary-level data and lessons are systematically incorporated into the project MEL system and used for programme improvement. Support mechanisms for capturing, tracking, analysing and reporting grievances and beneficiary feedback, and strengthen the integration of Grievance Redress System (GRS) evidence into monitoring, reporting and learning processes. Analyse local-level, pilot and beneficiary data to identify implementation and service-delivery gaps, inclusion and exclusion issues, targeting challenges and opportunities for institutionalization or scale-up. Support the SSPS policy and MEL interface for the Bangladesh Multidimensional Household Well-being Panel Survey, working with BBS, Cabinet Division, GED and other relevant stakeholders to articulate policy questions and use cases and ensure that survey evidence responds to social protection reform and programme learning needs. Support the use of survey and other pilot evidence for SDG localization, Family Card learning, social protection targeting and programme performance analysis, and development of decision-oriented evidence products and recommendations. Contribute, within the agreed institutional division of responsibilities, to joint technical processes relating to indicator frameworks, data access, privacy and ethics, analysis and publication planning, and methods review and learning. Translate evidence from pilots, beneficiary feedback and the household well-being survey into recommendations, analytical products and learning that support programme adaptation, policy dialogue and potential scale-up. 4- Lead Digital Knowledge, Evidence Platforms And Technology-Enabled Learning Lead the administration, maintenance, security, enhancement and continuous development of the National Website on Social Protection and related digital evidence platforms to support access to monitoring findings, research, dashboards, learning products and social protection knowledge. jobs.title: AI Application Engineer
jobs.description: Agentic Systems and Intelligent Automation Multiple Openings | Full-time About Ajentica Ajentica is an AI-native product engineering company helping ambitious software businesses become truly agentic. We partner with growth-stage and private-equity-backed companies to modernize complex platforms, redesign operational workflows and build intelligent systems that work alongside people, not merely generate content. Our work spans agentic automation, enterprise software modernization, intelligent product development and AI-enabled delivery across healthcare, pharmacy, HR technology and other operationally complex industries. From HIPAA-sensitive clinical workflows and autonomous desktop agents to platform integration and AI-assisted software development, we focus on moving AI beyond prototypes and into secure, measurable and production-ready systems. About the Role We are looking for well-rounded, highly capable software engineers who can apply AI to real business and engineering problems. This is not a prompt-engineering role, nor is it focused on developing foundational AI models. You will be a software engineer first, designing applications, services and workflows that use LLMs, multimodal models, and other AI capabilities where they create meaningful value. You may work on agentic workflows, intelligent automation, enterprise platform integration, software modernization, document processing, browser or desktop automation, knowledge retrieval and human-in-the-loop systems. The role requires both applied AI capability and meaningful depth in at least one broader area of software engineering (full-stack or backend development, distributed systems, data engineering, or devops). What You’ll Do Design, build and maintain production-grade AI-enabled applications and services. Translate business processes and operational problems into practical technical solutions. Integrate LLMs and other AI services with APIs, databases, enterprise platforms and existing software products. Build agentic workflows that can reason within defined boundaries, use tools and complete multi-step tasks. Develop backend services, APIs, event-driven processes and data pipelines supporting AI applications. Build retrieval and grounding solutions using structured and unstructured business data. Implement human review, approval and escalation mechanisms for sensitive or uncertain decisions. Design evaluations to measure accuracy, reliability, latency, cost and business outcomes. Implement logging, tracing, monitoring and observability for AI-enabled workflows. Handle model failures, unavailable services, incomplete data and other real-world exceptions safely. Write automated tests and participate in code reviews, architecture discussions and technical discovery. Take solutions from early investigation and prototyping through deployment, iteration and production support. Work closely with product managers, architects, domain experts and client engineering teams. Contribute to reusable engineering patterns, internal accelerators and Ajentica’s broader AI delivery capabilities. Core Qualifications A degree from a Tier 1 institution is strongly preferred. Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building production applications with significant usage. You are a fast, sharp thinker who accurately analyses problems, is skilled at clarifying ambiguous requirements, and possesses very strong English communication skills. You possess a high level of attention to detail and the proactiveness to flag issues and propose improvements. Proficiency in at least one production programming language, such as Python, TypeScript, C#, Java, or Go. Ability to work effectively with Python where required for AI application development. Familiarity with disciplined AI-based software development and the practices emerging around it. Experience designing and integrating APIs, services and databases. Understanding of system design, data modelling, testing and maintainable software architecture. Familiarity with Git, CI/CD, containerization and cloud deployment. Experience with monitoring, debugging and supporting applications in production. Ability to investigate ambiguous problems, test assumptions and make sound engineering trade-offs. Broader Engineering Depth Candidates should demonstrate meaningful experience in at least one of the following areas: Full-stack or backend engineering: Web applications, APIs, service architecture, authentication and modern application frameworks. Distributed systems: Event-driven systems, messaging, asynchronous processing, workflow orchestration and resilient services. Data engineering: Data pipelines, transformation, storage, search, data quality and analytical platforms. Cloud and DevOps engineering: Infrastructure, containers, CI/CD, deployment automation, observability, security and operational reliability. Candidates with exceptional depth in applied AI engineering will also be considered. Applied AI Experience Practical experience building applications using LLMs or other commercially available AI models. Experience with model APIs, structured outputs, function calling or tool use. Understanding of common agentic patterns, including workflow orchestration, routing, state management and human oversight. Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, semantic search or knowledge-grounded systems. Ability to assess when AI is appropriate and when conventional software or rules would be safer and more effective. Awareness of common AI application risks, including hallucination, prompt injection, unsafe tool use and unintended data exposure. Understanding of how to evaluate and improve AI application quality rather than relying solely on subjective demonstrations. Experience with frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen or similar platforms is helpful, but we value sound engineering judgement over familiarity with any particular framework. Nice to Have Experience integrating third-party OCR, document-processing, computer-vision or multimodal AI libraries/services. Browser automation, Windows desktop automation or UI automation experience. Experience with workflow engines, queues or distributed task-processing systems. Voice automation, speech-to-text, text-to-speech or IVR integration experience. Familiarity with MCP, tool registries or similar integration protocols. Experience developing software for healthcare, pharmacy, financial services or other regulated environments. Familiarity with HIPAA, PHI handling, data privacy, auditability or security-sensitive systems. Experience working directly with international clients or distributed engineering teams. What Good Looks Like You understand that an impressive prototype is only the beginning. A successful AI application must also be reliable, observable, secure, maintainable and commercially sensible. You do not reach for an LLM simply because one is available. You can distinguish between problems requiring AI, deterministic software, traditional automation or a combination of approaches. You are comfortable moving quickly during discovery while maintaining engineering discipline. You can explain your decisions, test your assumptions and take ownership of what you put into production. How We Work Ajentica follows an AI-first engineering approach. Our engineers use modern development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and equivalent platforms to accelerate investigation, development and testing. AI-assisted work must still be understood, validated and owned by the engineer. We value speed, but we place equal importance on accountability, technical judgement and software quality. What You’ll Get The opportunity to build AI applications for real operational environments. Exposure to international clients and complex enterprise problems. Ownership across discovery, architecture, implementation and production deployment. Opportunities to work across agentic systems, intelligent automation and modern software engineering. A growing engineering environment where strong contributors can influence technical standards, delivery practices and future products. How to Apply Please submit your CV or LinkedIn profile, along with links to your GitHub, portfolio or relevant projects where available. We would particularly like to hear about: A production software system you helped design or build. An AI-enabled application or automation you have implemented. The broader engineering area in which you have the strongest depth. Your individual contribution and the technical decisions you personally owned. Ajentica values demonstrated engineering ability over buzzwords. If you have built meaningful systems but do not meet every listed requirement, we would still like to hear from you.
